original_question: For a fixed integer m >= 1, define f(t) = 1/(e^{-mt}; e^{-2mt})_infty and define coefficients C_{m,n} by sum_{n>=0} C_{m,n} q^n = 1/(q^m; q^{2m})_infty, where (a; q)_infty := product_{j>=0} (1-a q^j). Can one obtain a local expansion of f(t) as t -> 0^+, beyond the leading bound and leading asymptotic term, so that one gets a full asymptotic expansion for the coefficients C_{m,n} rather than only the leading-term asymptotic?
target_in_paper: No direct match. arXiv:1606.04493 is a paper on open problems in two-dimensional conformal field theory and vertex operator algebras; the nearest official statement to your draft is Problem 2.2 in Section 2, which asks for convergence of intertwining-operator series needed to construct higher-genus correlation functions.
correct_elements: Your draft is mathematically coherent on its own terms: it fixes the parameter m, defines the generating function and coefficients C_{m,n}, and asks whether one can sharpen a leading asymptotic into a full asymptotic expansion by improving local analytic control. That general analytic posture is the only faint overlap with the cited paper. The actual paper, however, is not about q-series asymptotics or q-Pochhammer products.
missing_details: The draft does not use the paper's actual subject matter: rational two-dimensional conformal field theories constructed from vertex operator algebras.
It omits the central objects in the paper's Section 2: intertwining operators and the series built from them.
It omits the actual goal of the paper's nearest problem: constructing higher-genus chiral/full correlation functions.
It omits the governing framework explicitly named in Problem 2.1: the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal, and Moore-Seiberg.
It omits the geometric setting mentioned immediately after Problem 2.2: Teichmuller spaces and moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries.
It omits the reduction explained in Section 2: the remaining higher-genus part of Problem 2.1 is reduced to proving convergence of the intertwining-operator series.
It replaces the paper's VOA/CFT notation and hypotheses with unrelated q-series notation f(t), (a;q)_infty, and coefficients C_{m,n}.
It does not reflect that the paper is organized around Problems and Conjectures in Sections 2 through 8, rather than a q-series theorem/proposition chain.

If the intent was to match the paper faithfully, the correct ambient structures would include vertex operator algebras, graded state spaces, correlation functions, and higher-genus constructions, none of which appear in the draft.
refined_question: For a rational two-dimensional conformal field theory arising from a vertex operator algebra under the standard rationality assumptions used in the paper, can one prove the convergence of the higher-genus series obtained from intertwining operators, so that these series define higher-genus chiral correlation functions on the relevant Teichmuller/moduli spaces and thereby yield the corresponding higher-genus full correlation functions in the Kontsevich-Segal-Moore-Seiberg framework?
equivalent_formulation: Construct the higher-genus part of rational conformal field theories satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal, and Moore-Seiberg; in Section 2 the paper explicitly reduces this remaining part of Problem 2.1 to Problem 2.2, namely proving convergence of the intertwining-operator series.
justification: The supplied draft cannot be aligned with any q-series statement in arXiv:1606.04493. The paper's abstract and introduction describe a program on constructing and studying two-dimensional conformal field theories using the representation theory of vertex operator algebras. In Section 2, the paper identifies the main unresolved analytic issue as proving convergence of the higher-genus series built from intertwining operators, and explicitly states that the unresolved higher-genus part of Problem 2.1 is reduced to Problem 2.2. Therefore the closest paper-faithful replacement is Problem 2.2, not a question about asymptotic expansions of reciprocal q-Pochhammer products.
